questions.q: Hamlet, Laertes and Fortinbras have all lost fathers; Laertes and Fortinbras act at once, Hamlet delays. What are Laertes and Fortinbras doing structurally?
choices: Acting as foils that make Hamlet's hesitation stand out
questions.explain: Likeness in situation, difference in choice: the definition of a foil.

questions.q: A thriller's villain is a dim thug the hero beats easily. What would McKee's principle of antagonism predict?
choices: The audience will relax and enjoy the hero
The story is only as compelling as its opposition, so the victory will feel empty
questions.explain: A weak opponent means an easy, meaningless victory.

questions.q: A writer designs a hero, a main opponent and two secondary opponents, each standing for a different value and each in conflict with all the others. What is this?
questions.explain: Truby's tool for spreading conflict in many directions within the character web.

questions.q: In Racine's Phèdre, the nurse Oenone draws out Phèdre's secret love. Which role is she filling?
questions.explain: The confidant is the person the protagonist tells the truth to, so the audience hears it too.

questions.q: In a buddy-cop film, the partner shares the hero's goal of catching the gang, and his contrasting choices expose the hero's inner conflict. In Hauge's terms, he is the…
questions.explain: Hauge's reflection supports the hero's outer goal and helps reveal the inner conflict.

questions.q: Why do productions of Peter Pan traditionally have one actor play Mr Darling and Captain Hook?
choices: Barrie forbade doubling all other parts
The doubling makes meaning: the nursery's father returns as Neverland's villain
Hook has too few lines for a separate actor
questions.explain: Doubling can save money, but used well it makes a point about the characters.

questions.q: A feature on a factory closure picks a 'heartless executive', a 'loyal worker' and a 'wise union elder'. What's the risk?
choices: Casting real people as types because the structure needs them
questions.explain: Casting can be powerful, as in Lukas's Common Ground, but real people should be reported as individuals, not roles.

questions.q: Which statement about the ensemble is accurate?
choices: An ensemble has no structure, only mood
An ensemble must still have one clear protagonist
Only television can sustain an ensemble
In an ensemble, meaning comes from the pattern among characters, often variations on one want
questions.explain: Succession's siblings, Chekhov's sisters and The Wire's mirrored institutions all work by pattern.

ideas: Which approach defines each character by contrast with the others rather than one at a time?
Which approach says a protagonist can only be as compelling as the forces against them?
Which approach uses a character in a similar situation who chooses differently, to make another shine?
Which approach treats the cast list, and which roles one actor doubles, as a way of making meaning?
